notes:
The list is printed on n16.jpg (headed 'EAST OF SCOTLAND.' under the section title 'EAST COAST OF SCOTLAND.', with Shetland nos. 4–7 and Orkney nos. 8–14) and on n17.jpg (page 2: Mainland, nos. 15–29). It ends just above 'Diary from the Stations.' n18.jpg (page 3) has only diary text and no part of the list.

Columns, left to right: 'Returns in 8 years, including 1886.'; '1886. Actual returns.' (where an asterisk shows a return for 1886); the map number; the station and its county or locality; 'Values.' (migration value I–V); and 'Feet.' Orkney stations and Sumburgh Head have no height. Carr Rock and Fidra have '?' for both value and height. The 'Returns' column gives '1st' for Noss Head and Girdleness, meaning their first return. In 'other' I tagged each figure with its column heading. Those labels are mine and are not printed.

No keepers are named in the list. A sideways note runs down the right margin of both pages: 'The names of the Reporters are given under “Diary from the Stations.”' So for this year the keepers' names have to come from the diary (for example, 'N. Unst.—John Nichol (principal)' on n17).

Marks: the asterisks match the introduction, which says twelve stations sent returns. Eleven asterisks are clearly printed: N. Unst, Sumburgh Head, N. Ronaldshay, Dunnet Head, Noss Head, Cromarty, Girdleness, Bell Rock, Isle of May, Inchkeith and Fidra. The twelfth must be Pentland Skerries, whose mark is only a faint broken stroke. The text also says Pentland Skerries sent nine schedules in 1886. Auskerry and Chanonry Point have counts in the 8-year column (6 and 4) but no 1886 asterisk. The braces beside Carr Rock (26B) and Fidra (28B) only join their two-line entries to the '?' values. They are not markers of meaning. Both 'B's are small capitals ('26B.', '28B.'). The introduction says Carr Rock and the Tay Lightship were not sent schedules this year. Tay Lightship is not in the list at all.

Spellings copied as printed: 'Whalsey Skerries' (now Whalsay), 'N. Ronaldshay', 'Girdleness' and 'Montroseness' each as one word, and 'Cromarty, East Cromarty'. Chanonry Point is printed with the county 'Elgin', although it is on the Black Isle in Ross/Cromarty. That is probably a slip in the print. It agrees with the earlier finding that the 1879 print has a slip at Chanonry Point. St Abb's Head is set tightly as 'StAbb's Head,Berwickshire,'. I have written it with normal spaces. The dotted leaders in 'printed' are only approximately the printed length. The OCR misreads several values ('Wi.', 'We', 'Va', 'ie', 'LV.') and gives '98p.' for 28B. All of these were read from the images instead. No light characters are given in this list.
